en stakkel.explanation: "En stakkel" means "a poor thing". To feel sorry for a named person, put "stakkels" (poor) before the name: "Stakkels Peter!" (Poor Peter!)

en stald.explanation: "En stald" means "a stable". To say where the cows are, use "i stalden" (in the stable): "Køerne står i stalden" (The cows are in the stable).

en stamme.explanation: "En stamme" means "a tribe / trunk". When you talk about a group of people with a shared language and way of life, it means "a tribe": "En stamme bor i junglen" (A tribe lives in the jungle). When you talk about the thick main part of a tree, it means "a trunk": "Katten klatrer op ad stammen" (The cat climbs up the trunk). The verb "at stamme" (to stutter) is spelled the same: "Han stammer, når han er nervøs" (He stutters when he is nervous).

en stand.explanation: "En stand" means "a stand / booth". To describe the condition of something, use "i god stand" (in good condition): "Cyklen er i god stand" (The bike is in good condition).

en stank.explanation: "En stank" means "a stench". To talk about a smell that is neither good nor bad, use "en lugt" (a smell): "Der er en lugt af kaffe" (There is a smell of coffee).

en startup.explanation: "En startup" means "a startup". It comes from the English word "startup". To say where someone works, use "i": "Han arbejder i en startup" (He works in a startup).

en stat.explanation: "En stat" means "a state", as in a country or a part of a country. To talk about the national government, use "staten" (the state): "Skatten går til staten" (The tax goes to the state).

en station.explanation: "En station" means "a station". To say where you meet someone, use "på" (at) before "stationen" (the station): "Vi mødes på stationen" (We meet at the station).

en statistik.explanation: "En statistik" means "a statistic". To talk about the school subject, leave out "en": "Hun læser statistik" (She studies statistics).

en statsadvokat.explanation: "En statsadvokat" means "a public prosecutor". It is built from "stat" (state) and "en advokat" (a lawyer). To talk about the lawyer who speaks for the accused, use "en forsvarer" (a defense lawyer): "Forsvareren taler for den anklagede" (The defense lawyer speaks for the accused).

en statsleder.explanation: "En statsleder" means "a head of state". In Denmark, the head of state is the monarch. To talk about the person who leads the government, use "en statsminister" (a prime minister): "Statsministeren leder regeringen" (The prime minister leads the government).

en statsminister.explanation: "En statsminister" means "a prime minister". It is built from "stat" (state) and "en minister" (a minister). To say what someone's job is, leave out "en" after "er": "Hun er statsminister" (She is the prime minister).

en statue.explanation: "En statue" means "a statue". A famous statue in Copenhagen is "Den lille havfrue" (The Little Mermaid). To say a statue is put up, use "at rejse" (to raise): "De rejser en statue på torvet" (They put up a statue in the square).

en status.explanation: "En status" means "a status". To ask how a project is going, say: "Hvad er status på projektet?" (What is the status of the project?). To talk about a short progress update at work, say: "Vi laver en status hver fredag" (We do a status update every Friday).

en stavelse.explanation: "En stavelse" means "a syllable". To say how many syllables a word has, say: "Ordet har to stavelser" (The word has two syllables).

en stedfar.explanation: "En stedfar" means "a stepfather". It is built from "sted-" (step) and "far" (father). The same "sted-" starts "en stedsøster" (a stepsister): "Hun er min stedsøster" (She is my stepsister).

en stedmor.explanation: "En stedmor" means "a stepmother". It is built from "sted-" (step) and "mor" (mother). The same "sted-" starts "en stedsøster" (a stepsister): "Hun er min stedsøster" (She is my stepsister).

en stegepande.explanation: "En stegepande" means "a frying pan". It is built from "at stege" (to fry) and "en pande" (a pan). To say it in a short way, use "panden" (the pan): "Læg kødet på panden" (Put the meat in the pan).

en stegning.explanation: "En stegning" means "a frying". It comes from the verb "at stege" (to fry). To say you fry food, use the verb: "Jeg steger kødet i smør" (I fry the meat in butter).

en stemme.explanation: "En stemme" means "a voice / a vote". When you talk about how someone sounds, it means "a voice": "Hun har en dyb stemme" (She has a deep voice). When you talk about one person's choice in an election, it means "a vote": "Hver stemme tæller" (Every vote counts). To say you vote, use the verb "at stemme": "Jeg stemmer i morgen" (I vote tomorrow).

en stemmeseddel.explanation: "En stemmeseddel" means "a ballot". It is built from "en stemme" (a vote) and "en seddel" (a slip of paper). The same "seddel" ends "en pengeseddel" (a banknote): "Jeg har en pengeseddel på hundrede kroner" (I have a hundred-kroner banknote).

en stemning.explanation: "En stemning" means "a mood / atmosphere". To say a gathering feels pleasant, use "god stemning" (good atmosphere): "Der var god stemning til festen" (There was a good atmosphere at the party). To talk about one person's mood, use "et humør" (a mood): "Hun er i godt humør" (She is in a good mood).

en sten.explanation: "En sten" means "a stone". To say people throw stones, use "at kaste" (to throw) and leave out "en": "Børnene kaster sten i søen" (The children throw stones into the lake).

en stewardesse.explanation: "En stewardesse" means "a flight attendant". To say a man has this job, use "en steward" (a male flight attendant): "Min bror er steward" (My brother is a flight attendant).

en sti.explanation: "En sti" means "a path". To talk about the road that cars drive on, use "en vej" (a road): "Bilerne kører på vejen" (The cars drive on the road).

en stige.explanation: "En stige" means "a ladder". The verb "at stige" (to rise) is spelled the same. To say a price is going up, say: "Prisen stiger" (The price is going up).

en stigning.explanation: "En stigning" means "a rise / increase". When you talk about a slope that climbs, it means "a grade": "Bakken har en stigning på ti procent" (The hill has a ten percent grade). For the opposite, use "et fald" (a drop): "Der var et fald i temperaturen" (There was a drop in the temperature).

en stikdåse.explanation: "En stikdåse" means "a power strip". To talk about the socket in the wall that the power strip is plugged into, use "en stikkontakt" (a wall outlet): "Stikdåsen er sat i stikkontakten" (The power strip is plugged into the wall outlet).

en stikkontakt.explanation: "En stikkontakt" means "an outlet". To talk about the part that you push into the outlet, use "et stik" (a plug): "Sæt stikket i stikkontakten" (Put the plug in the outlet).

en stikling.explanation: "En stikling" means "a cutting". To say you take cuttings from a plant, use "at tage stiklinger" (to take cuttings): "Jeg tager stiklinger fra planten" (I take cuttings from the plant).

en stil.explanation: "En stil" means "a style". At school, "en stil" also means "an essay": "Vi skriver en stil i dansk" (We write an essay in Danish class).

en stilling.explanation: "En stilling" means "a position / job". To say you are applying for a job, use "at søge" (to apply for) before it: "Jeg søger en stilling som lærer" (I am applying for a job as a teacher). In sports, it also means "the score": "Stillingen er 2-1" (The score is 2-1).

en stillingsannonce.explanation: "En stillingsannonce" means "a job ad". It is built from "en stilling" (a job) and "en annonce" (an ad).

en stirren.explanation: "En stirren" means "a stare". It comes from the verb "at stirre" (to stare). To ask someone why they look at you so hard, say: "Hvorfor stirrer du på mig?" (Why are you staring at me?)

en stjerne.explanation: "En stjerne" means "a star". To say how good a hotel is, use the number of stars: "Hotellet har fem stjerner" (The hotel has five stars).

en stol.explanation: "En stol" means "a chair". To tell someone to sit down, use "på" (on): "Sæt dig på stolen" (Sit down on the chair).

en storby.explanation: "En storby" means "a big city". It is built from "stor" (big) and "en by" (a town). To talk about a small place in the countryside, use "en landsby" (a village): "Min bedstemor bor i en lille landsby" (My grandmother lives in a small village).

en storebror.explanation: "En storebror" means "a big brother". It is built from "stor" (big) and "bror" (brother). To talk about a younger brother, use "en lillebror" (a little brother): "Min lillebror er syv år" (My little brother is seven years old).

en storesøster.explanation: "En storesøster" means "a big sister". It is built from "stor" (big) and "søster" (sister). To talk about a younger sister, use "en lillesøster" (a little sister): "Min lillesøster er syv år" (My little sister is seven years old).

en storfamilie.explanation: "En storfamilie" means "an extended family". It is built from "stor" (big) and "en familie" (a family). To talk about only parents and children, use "en kernefamilie" (a nuclear family): "Vi er en kernefamilie med mor, far og to børn" (We are a nuclear family with mom, dad and two children).

en stork.explanation: "En stork" means "a stork". Hans Christian Andersen, a Danish writer, wrote a fairy tale called "Storkene" (The Storks).

en storm.explanation: "En storm" means "a storm". To say a storm is raging, say: "Stormen raser ude" (The storm is raging outside).

en stormflod.explanation: "En stormflod" means "a storm surge". To report a weather warning, say: "Der er varsel om stormflod i nat" (There is a storm surge warning tonight).

en straf.explanation: "En straf" means "a punishment". To say someone is punished, use "at få" (to get) before it: "Han fik en hård straf" (He got a harsh punishment).

en straffeattest.explanation: "En straffeattest" means "a criminal record". It is built from "en straf" (a punishment) and "en attest" (a certificate).

en strand.explanation: "En strand" means "a beach". To say you are at the beach, use "på" (on), not "i" (in): "Vi er på stranden" (We are at the beach).

en strandpromenade.explanation: "En strandpromenade" means "a beach promenade". It is built from "en strand" (a beach) and "en promenade" (a promenade).

en strandtur.explanation: "En strandtur" means "a trip to the beach". It is built from "en strand" (a beach) and "en tur" (a trip). The same "tur" ends "en cykeltur" (a bike ride): "Vi tager på cykeltur i morgen" (We are going on a bike ride tomorrow).

en strategi.explanation: "En strategi" means "a strategy". To talk about one move at a certain moment, use "en taktik" (a tactic): "Hans taktik var at vente" (His tactic was to wait).

en streamingtjeneste.explanation: "En streamingtjeneste" means "a streaming service". It is built from "streaming" (streaming) and "en tjeneste" (a service). "En tjeneste" also means "a favor": "Kan du gøre mig en tjeneste?" (Can you do me a favor?)

en streg.explanation: "En streg" means "a line / stroke". When a surprise ruins a plan, Danes say "en streg i regningen" (literally, "a line in the bill"): "Regnen var en streg i regningen for vores picnic" (The rain ruined our picnic).

en strejke.explanation: "En strejke" means "a strike", as in workers who stop working. To say workers go on strike, use the verb "at strejke" (to strike): "De vil strejke" (They will go on strike).

en strid.explanation: "En strid" means "a dispute / conflict". To say something goes against a rule, use "i strid med" (in conflict with): "Det er i strid med reglerne" (It is against the rules).

en strikhue.explanation: "En strikhue" means "a knitted hat". It is built from "at strikke" (to knit) and "en hue" (a hat).

en strofe.explanation: "En strofe" means "a stanza". To point to a part of a poem, say which stanza it is: "Læs anden strofe højt" (Read the second stanza aloud).

en strube.explanation: "En strube" means "a throat". To talk about the neck, use "en hals" (a neck): "Han har en lang hals" (He has a long neck).

en struktur.explanation: "En struktur" means "a structure". The verb "at strukturere" (to structure) goes with it: "Jeg strukturerer min dag" (I structure my day).

en strygning.explanation: "En strygning" means "an ironing". It comes from the verb "at stryge" (to iron). To say you iron clothes, use the verb: "Jeg stryger skjorten" (I iron the shirt).

en strømpe.explanation: "En strømpe" means "a stocking / sock". Danes also say "en sok" (a sock): "Jeg har et hul i min sok" (I have a hole in my sock).

en studentereksamen.explanation: "En studentereksamen" means "a high school diploma". In Denmark, you take it at the end of three years at "et gymnasium" (an upper secondary school). To say someone has passed it, use "student": "Hun er student" (She has passed her final exams).

en studenterfest.explanation: "En studenterfest" means "a graduation party". It is built from "en student" (a school graduate) and "en fest" (a party).

en studenterhue.explanation: "En studenterhue" means "a graduation cap". In Denmark, it is a white cap that young people put on after passing their final school exams.

en studerende.explanation: "En studerende" means "a student". To talk about a child at school, use "en elev" (a pupil): "Min datter er elev i tredje klasse" (My daughter is a pupil in third grade).

en studiegruppe.explanation: "En studiegruppe" means "a study group". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en gruppe" (a group).

en studiekammerat.explanation: "En studiekammerat" means "a fellow student". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en kammerat" (a pal).

en studieplan.explanation: "En studieplan" means "a study plan". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en plan" (a plan).

en studieretning.explanation: "En studieretning" means "a field of study". In Denmark, it is the line you choose at "et gymnasium" (an upper secondary school), such as languages or science.

en studietur.explanation: "En studietur" means "a study trip". It is built from "et studie" (a study) and "en tur" (a trip).

en stue.explanation: "En stue" means "a living room". The same "stue" is in "stueetagen" (the ground floor): "Vi bor i stueetagen" (We live on the ground floor).

en stund.explanation: "En stund" means "a while". To say you waited a bit, say: "Vi ventede en stund" (We waited for a while). To describe a quiet moment, add a describing word: "en rolig stund" (a calm spell).

en styrelse.explanation: "En styrelse" means "an agency". An example is "Sundhedsstyrelsen" (the Danish Health Authority).

en styrke.explanation: "En styrke" means "a strength". To talk about physical power, say: "Han har stor styrke i armene" (He has great strength in his arms).

en størrelse.explanation: "En størrelse" means "a size". It comes from "stor" (big). To ask about someone's size, say: "Hvilken størrelse bruger du?" (What size do you wear?)

en støtte.explanation: "En støtte" means "a support". When you talk about money that someone receives, it means "financial support": "Hun får støtte fra staten" (She gets support from the state).

en støvle.explanation: "En støvle" means "a boot". To talk about boots as a pair, say: "et par støvler" (a pair of boots). The word is also in "gummistøvler" (rubber boots): "Jeg tager gummistøvler på i regnvejr" (I put on rubber boots in rainy weather).

en støvsuger.explanation: "En støvsuger" means "a vacuum cleaner". It is built from "støv" (dust) and "suger" (sucker), which comes from "at suge" (to suck). To say you vacuum, use the verb "at støvsuge": "Han støvsuger hver lørdag" (He vacuums every Saturday).

en støvsugning.explanation: "En støvsugning" means "a vacuuming". It comes from the verb "at støvsuge" (to vacuum). To say you vacuum before guests come, say: "Jeg støvsuger, før gæsterne kommer" (I vacuum before the guests arrive).

en succes.explanation: "En succes" means "a success". To say someone is successful, leave out "en": "Han har succes som forfatter" (He is successful as an author).

en suite.explanation: "En suite" means "a suite". To talk about an ordinary hotel room, use "et værelse" (a room): "Vi har et værelse med to senge" (We have a room with two beds).

en sukkerskål.explanation: "En sukkerskål" means "a sugar bowl". It is built from "sukker" (sugar) and "en skål" (a bowl). The same "skål" is what you say when you raise a glass: "Skål!" (Cheers!)

en sum.explanation: "En sum" means "a sum". When you add numbers, "summen" (the sum) is the result: "Summen af to og tre er fem" (The sum of two and three is five).

en sundhedsplejerske.explanation: "En sundhedsplejerske" means "a health visitor". It is built from "sundhed" (health) and "pleje" (care). In Denmark, a health visitor comes to see new families after a baby is born.

en suppe.explanation: "En suppe" means "a soup". A soup is named after its main ingredient, as in "tomatsuppe" (tomato soup): "Der er tomatsuppe til middag" (There is tomato soup for dinner).

en sut.explanation: "En sut" means "a pacifier". To say a baby sucks on it, use "at sutte på" (to suck on): "Babyen sutter på sin sut" (The baby sucks on its pacifier).

en sutteflaske.explanation: "En sutteflaske" means "a baby bottle". It is built from "at sutte" (to suck) and "en flaske" (a bottle).

en svaghed.explanation: "En svaghed" means "a weakness". To say you cannot resist something, use "at have en svaghed for" (to have a weakness for): "Jeg har en svaghed for chokolade" (I have a weakness for chocolate).

en svamp.explanation: "En svamp" means "a mushroom / fungus". When you talk about picking mushrooms, use the plural "svampe": "Jeg plukker svampe om efteråret" (I pick mushrooms in the fall). When you talk about washing dishes, "en svamp" means "a sponge": "Jeg vasker op med en svamp" (I wash up with a sponge).

en svane.explanation: "En svane" means "a swan". The "knopsvane" (mute swan) is the national bird of Denmark. A young swan is "en svaneunge" (a cygnet): "Svaneungen følger efter moren" (The cygnet follows its mother).

en svans.explanation: "En svans" means "a tail". An animal's tail is also "en hale" (a tail): "Hunden logrer med halen" (The dog wags its tail).

en svensker.explanation: "En svensker" means "a Swede". It comes from "Sverige" (Sweden). To talk about something Swedish, use "svensk" (Swedish): "en svensk bil" (a Swedish car).

en svigerdatter.explanation: "En svigerdatter" means "a daughter-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "en datter" (a daughter).

en svigerfar.explanation: "En svigerfar" means "a father-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "far" (father).

en svigerinde.explanation: "En svigerinde" means "a sister-in-law". To talk about a brother-in-law, use "en svoger" (a brother-in-law): "Hendes svoger bor i Aalborg" (Her brother-in-law lives in Aalborg).

en svigermor.explanation: "En svigermor" means "a mother-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "mor" (mother).

en svigersøn.explanation: "En svigersøn" means "a son-in-law". It is built from "sviger-" (in-law) and "en søn" (a son).

en svindler.explanation: "En svindler" means "a swindler". To say someone cheated you out of money, use the verb "at svindle" (to cheat): "Han svindlede mig for tusind kroner" (He cheated me out of a thousand kroner).

en svinestald.explanation: "En svinestald" means "a pigsty". It is built from "et svin" (a pig) and "en stald" (a stable for farm animals).

en svoger.explanation: "En svoger" means "a brother-in-law". To talk about a sister-in-law, use "en svigerinde" (a sister-in-law): "Min svigerinde bor i Odense" (My sister-in-law lives in Odense).

en sværm.explanation: "En sværm" means "a swarm". To talk about many fans around a star, use "en sværm af" (a swarm of): "En sværm af fans ventede foran hotellet" (A swarm of fans waited in front of the hotel).

en svømmebane.explanation: "En svømmebane" means "a swimming lane". It is built from "at svømme" (to swim) and "en bane" (a track).
